bullets.section: What I’m reading and putting to use
bullets.title: Back Mechanic
bullets.creator: Dr
bullets.note: , one of the great Jedis of spine mechanics. The description: “_Back Mechanic_ guides you through a self-assessment of your pain triggers then shows you how to avoid these roadblocks to recovery. Then, effective exercises are coached in a step-by-step progressive plan. Spine expert Prof. McGill used his 30 years of research findings and clinical investigations to create this evidence-based guide that has helped thousands reclaim their lives.” Long-term readers might recognize Stuart’s name, as I featured the following exercises from him in a previous 5BF: “[Enhancing low back health through stabilization exercise](https://www.ahs.uwaterloo.ca/~mcgill/fitnessleadersguide.pdf).” From extreme pain six months ago, these exercises helped me to aggressively ski half-day sessions 4–5x/week all of January and February.

bullets.title: Power Broker #01: Robert Caro
bullets.creator: 99% Invisible_, hosted by Roman Mars and Elliott Kalan
bullets.note:
, hosted by [Roman Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Mars) and [Elliott Kalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Kalan). This is spectacular. I must confess with great shame that I have never finished [_The Power Broker_](https://www.amazon.com/Power-Broker-Robert-Moses-Fall/dp/0394720245/)_,_ the legendary Pulitzer Prize winner by Robert Caro. Dozens of my most brilliant friends have recommended it, and I’ve tried valiantly, but I somehow fall short. The book chronicles the life of Robert Moses, a city planner who became the most powerful man in New York, shaping the city’s politics and infrastructure.  
​  
This three-part podcast allowed me to salvage my self-respect and dive back into what I knew to be an incredible story worth exploring. It also reignited my desire to finish the book.  
​  
Listen on [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/power-broker-01-robert-caro/id394775318?i=1000642195418), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/6nRsxCu5n0Z8xBF63OGI1n?si=F_JYXAfQQi-mJDzOR511AA), or wherever you get your podcasts. I will be listening to episodes #2 and #3 in the series over the weekend. To sample Robert Caro’s incredible writing, read the “if you do everything” paragraph [here](https://www.dwarkeshpatel.com/p/lyndon-johnson).  
​  
For a cinematic impression of Robert Moses, you can find a creative variant of him in Edward Norton’s brilliant adaptation of [_Motherless Brooklyn_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motherless_Brooklyn_(novel)) as Moses Randolph. [The trailer here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fru8IkuDp_k)—and the entire film—is well worth watching.

bullets.title: Humanitarians of Tinder
bullets.note: Since I’m back on the dating scene, I decided to revisit this old gem. After a hard day, it’s a great way to laugh until it hurts and go to bed with a smile. Life is absurd, and sometimes you just need to bathe in the “WTF?” of it all.

bullets.title: How to Start a War
bullets.note: “How to Start a War” is my first published fiction piece, and it’s the first time I’ve shared fiction on the blog. It’s a short story about mercenaries, modern life, and the games we play. How much of it is actually fiction? Well, that’s a damn good question. [Read it here](https://tim.blog/2024/03/22/how-to-start-a-war/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf#content), and let me know what you think in the blog post’s comments.
